text:
Macklin Celebrini is making history on a team that isn't ready to win yet. He reached 200 career points this month, and the headlines are a mix of admiration and pleading: be patient, help is coming. The Sharks are 9-11-2 with 20 points, and our playoff odds sit at 8%.

The chances explain why. San Jose has taken under 44% of all expected goals (the quality of chances) and 45% at five on five, allows 3.86 expected goals per 60 minutes, and its penalty kill gives up over one expected goal a game. Both pairs that play the most, Darnell Nurse with Michael Kesselring and Jacob Trouba with rookie Sam Dickinson, are underwater. The team has been finishing about 11 goals below its chances and getting about ten goals of help from its goalies, so the record is roughly honest.

The future is the story, and it's arriving early. Celebrini with Will Smith and Igor Chernyshov has taken 62% of the chances. Rookie Ivar Stenberg has been called the one thing going right, won an eight-round shootout, and hit three posts in another game. Dickinson is getting the top power-play job. Yaroslav Askarov's hot start has the team believing it's real. Mason Marchment scored his 100th career goal, and Dmitry Orlov is running hot with nine points in ten.

What we'd watch: how the Celebrini, Smith and Stenberg minutes develop, because this season is about building the thing, not finishing it.
